turns.learner: Hello teacher! I want to practise talking about things around me, like my room.
turns.tutor: Hello! Great idea. Let's talk about your room. Tell me two sentences about things in your room. For example: "I have a dog. The dog is brown." Now you try!

turns.learner: I have a bed in my room. A bed is big and very comfortable.
turns.tutor: Nice sentences! Look at the second one. You already said "a bed", so we say "The bed is big." Use "the" when we talk about the same thing again. Can you say it again?

turns.learner: Ok. I have a bed. The bed is big. But I think a is also okay, no?
turns.tutor: Good, "The bed is big" is correct! "A bed is big" sounds like any bed, a new one. But you mean your bed, the one we already know. So we use "the". Now try: I have a desk. ___ desk is small.

turns.learner: I have a desk. A desk is small. Maybe the? I am not sure, both look correct to me.
turns.tutor: Your first idea, "the", is right! Think: "I have a desk" is the first time. Then it is the same desk, so "The desk is small." Rule: first time = a/an, second time = the. Try: I see an apple. ___ apple is red.

turns.learner: The apple is red. So first time a, second time the. Is it the same for my phone?
turns.tutor: Yes, exactly! "The apple is red" is correct. It is the same for your phone: "I have a phone. The phone is new." Now you try: write two sentences about a thing in your room.

turns.learner: I have a lamp in my room. The lamp is on the desk.
turns.tutor: Perfect! "I have a lamp. The lamp is on the desk." Both sentences are correct. Last one: write a or an. I see ___ orange on the table.
